text: "Nothing at any time--nothing," he answered, firmly. It would have been folly to have disbelieved the truthful look of his wondering face, and she turned away in amazement and confusion. There was a long pause. "I hope, Mrs. Miller, you will not refuse any assistance I can render to your child," he said, at length. She started, and replied, tremblingly and confusedly, "No, sir; we shall be grateful to you, if you can save her"--and went quickly, with a strange abstraction on her white face, into the inner room.

provenance.work: The Ghost Stories of an Antiquary
